rationale: Version 10 (drafted 2026-11-18 on the operator's three decisions of that day; docs/records/evals/2026-11-18-release-requirements-v10.md) records three decisions and keeps every other v9 value. It is a new version rather than an amendment of v9, because v9 was read: lane AF scored both v9 roles for 10.8.0, the county pair and the v8.7.0 seeds 42 and 43, and section 6.5 of HOLDOUT_AND_EVALUATION records every confirmation read in the next version's rationale. Drafted 2026-11-18, registered the same day. (1) postal_unit is judged as a no-loss check against the published model: it registers maxLoss 0 and no minimum, on the comparative rows and with the cluster-robust difference bound po_box_cedex's loss check uses. Under v9 its minimum of 0.85 failed every arm, the published model's own included (10.8.0 0.725 development and 0.720 confirmation, seed 42 0.825 and 0.815, seed 43 0.771 and 0.765), so it judged the published deficiency rather than the change. The Bonferroni family stays at 16 checks: postal_unit's minimum check is replaced by its loss check. (2) IE counties are region. WOF holds the 26 counties an Irish address writes (Co. Westmeath, Co. Dublin) as region places and the 31 local authorities as county places, and the gauntlet board tags Co. Westmeath region. The codex county-designators table now gives each country's county tag (US and CA subregion, IE region), and heldout/dataset/relabel.run.ts revision county-designator-codex-tag relabeled the 2 IE gleif-lei development rows (co Dublin) from subregion to region: heldout-dev-v0.8.18 adeeef40d7d81a7c to 771811f7a5a8e4da. The confirmation and both probe collections hold no IE row with a county designator. (3) The confirmation role keeps v9's collections, heldout-confirm-v0.8.18@681959088a46e5c6 with heldout-confirm-v0.8.19-probes-r2@8d423f96f9d5a1d4 (operator decision 2026-11-18). Confirmation reads before registration: under v8, v8.7.0 seed 42 read heldout-confirm-v0.8.18 (version 8606834b12100089) on 2026-11-16 with its postal card (fail), its shaped card and the fixed postcode repair (insufficient evidence); under v9 on 2026-11-17 (lane AF, docs/records/evals/2026-11-17-release-requirements-v9.md section 5), 10.8.0's baseline scoring of both v9 confirmation collections (fail, from postal_unit), countyDesignatorFallback on against off (fail, from postal_unit), seed 42 n42-i8 (fail) and seed 43 n43-i8 (fail). Under section 6.5 the failed candidate reads retire these rows for recipe selection: no recipe, seed, checkpoint or decoder choice may be made by comparing their confirmation results, and the rows are read only for the release decision of a candidate already chosen on development, each read recorded in the next version's rationale. Their successor is drawn from the v0.8.20 corpus split, which holds out new groups, and frozen before the next release-directed run.

requirements.reason: Issue #2764: cited operator rules for FR (SP 8855 lines 2 and 3), GB (PAF Sub Building Name), IT (scala, piano, interno on line 3), AU (FLAT/UNIT TYPE table) and NZ (ADV358 Unit Type), with only designators no training recipe draws. A row whose expected spans hold a venue is left out: the FR named complexes (RESIDENCE, LOTISSEMENT), labeled venue since recipe fix 48fca721dd, carry no unit span, so they don't test this task.
requirements.maxLossReason: The operator decided on 2026-11-18 that a release mustn't lose this capability against the published model, which reads it below any registered minimum: no training recipe draws these designators, so the rate a candidate reaches measures the corpus, and the release decides only whether the change loses it. No loss is the objective's own threshold (minimumImprovement 0), so an arm whose difference interval reaches below zero reads insufficient evidence, as the objective does.

requirements.task: Resolving an ordinary address to the components and admin places its answer key gives, on the geocode path production runs
requirements.reason: A change that acts only in the resolver, such as countyDesignatorFallback, leaves every exact-parse outcome equal, so no other check can judge it (lane Y, docs/records/evals/2026-11-17-county-fallback-and-arabic-fold.md). The outcome is heldout/per/geocode-outcome's: the resolved components and every written locality, dependent locality, subregion, region and country placed at its tag.
requirements.maxLossReason: The objective admits no exact-parse loss in the equal-country rate (minimumImprovement 0). The geocode outcome is bounded at one point of the same equal-country rate. A model change reads the comparative rows, so the bound inherits the objective's width; a resolver change, with one model in both arms, reads every recorded class and its bound decides at one point.

inference.description: HELDOUT_INFERENCE_RULE in heldout/per/country.ts (served-locale-package): each row is parsed by the shipped Latin locale package for its country (release.config.json locales), falling back to en-us, with the row's country as localeHint; a package whose loader reports an unfed required channel is refused. The verdict records the rule and the rows each package parsed.

statistics.groupingAssumption: A row's independent unit is its group within its country: base_source_id when derived, else source_id. Rows are not declared independent, so a check that reads an ungrouped row is insufficient evidence. Limitation: structure shared across groups (one source's conventions, one place's many addresses) is not modelled. The dataset quota counts groups, not rows, against 1,000 per country.
